subject: Medford High School Project Update
overview: School Committee Vice Chair Jenny Graham provided a status update on the Medford High School Project's feasibility study and MSBA reimbursement process. The discussion detailed the financial and educational benefits of a new facility versus the cost of deferred maintenance.

items.title: Guest Introduction and Personal Background
items.summary: Host John Petrella introduced Jenny Graham, Vice Chair of the School Committee and Chair of the Medford High School Project, to discuss the ongoing building initiative.

items.title: Project Status and MSBA Feasibility Phase
items.summary: Graham reported that the project is currently in the feasibility phase with the MSBA and expects to narrow down design options to a single choice by June.

items.title: Educational Goals and Community Facility Integration
items.summary: The proposed project aims to consolidate Pre-K programs and the Curtis Tufts school onto one campus to relieve overcrowding in elementary schools. Graham noted that simply bringing the current building up to code would cost $438 million without eligibility for MSBA reimbursement.

items.title: Project Cost Components and Financing
items.summary: Current estimates include construction materials, labor, and contingencies, but exclude bond interest and potential tax calculations for residents. Graham stated the project is not expected to necessitate changes to the existing teacher's union contract.

items.title: MSBA Reimbursement Formula
items.summary: Graham explained that the MSBA's statutory reimbursement formula is based on community wealth and maintenance practices, with the current feasibility phase being reimbursed at approximately 53%.

items.title: Owner's Project Manager and Designer Selection
items.summary: The city has hired Lefebvre as the Owner's Project Manager and SMMA as the project designer, both of whom have experience with large-scale comprehensive high school builds.

items.title: Design Selection Metrics and Community Input
items.summary: A 15-member voting committee is using community forums and resident feedback to narrow 29 design options down to a final selection. Graham emphasized maximizing space value and improving the learning environment as primary metrics for the final choice.
